title: The UNSIGNED attribute
context: What is the UNSIGNED attribute on integer columns for?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): MySQL questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: UNSIGNED removes the negative range and doubles the positive range. For example, TINYINT has -128 to 127, while TINYINT UNSIGNED has 0 to 255. Use it for values that can never be negative, such as counts, IDs or ages, when you need the extra room. Be careful with arithmetic: subtracting past zero on an UNSIGNED column raises an out-of-range error in strict mode, instead of going negative.

points.title: Doubled range
points.why: UNSIGNED gives twice the positive range at the same storage size.

points.title: Subtraction underflow
points.why: Subtracting below zero on an UNSIGNED column is an error, which surprises people.
